newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly weaker, key inverse widens.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly weaker, key inverse widens.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mostly lower in sluggish dealings Tuesday, with the key December/March inversion widening further because of firmness in the cash market, traders said.

"Cash premiums continue to stay high," a KCBT trader said. "That showed up in the Dec/March spread, which opened at around 20 cents (per bushel) and widened late to 23 cents before settling at 22 cents."
Cash basis bids firmed overnight at locations in eastern Kansas as domestic demand remained strong but producers held off from selling their supplies of HRW wheat.
"The market continues to act rather erratically, trading a couple of cents on both sides of unchanged while it tries to find some kind of input," another trader said.
KCBT wheat settled unchanged to six cents per bushel lower, with Dec unchanged at $4.38-3/4.

The players' sheet showed CIS bought 1.2 million Dec bushels and sold 800,000 Dec and 900,000 March. CIS also bull-spread 700,000 Dec/March at 21-1/2 cents. Prudential sold 800,000 Dec and 1.2 million March. FIMAT bear-spread 600 March/Dec at between 21 to 23 cents per bushels.
